items.followUp: Describe the structure and function of red blood cells.

rubric.why: White blood cells protect the body from pathogens.
rubric.description: State their protective role against pathogens.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking protection of the body to pathogens.

rubric.why: Phagocytosis is one way white blood cells destroy pathogens.
rubric.description: Explain that white blood cells engulf pathogens by phagocytosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing engulfment by phagocytosis.

rubric.why: Lymphocytes produce antibodies that help fight pathogens.
rubric.description: State that some white blood cells produce antibodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying lymphocytes and antibody production.

rubric.why: White blood cells have a nucleus and can move out of blood vessels to reach affected tissues.
rubric.description: Give a structural feature and explain how white blood cells reach tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they have a nucleus and 1 mark for stating that they can move out of blood vessels.

modelAnswer: White blood cells, also called leucocytes, protect the body against pathogens and disease.
They can move out of blood vessels and engulf pathogens by phagocytosis.
Some white blood cells, such as lymphocytes, produce antibodies that help destroy pathogens.
White blood cells have a nucleus and do not contain haemoglobin.

items.followUp: State four advantages of using scientific names for organisms.

rubric.why: A binomial name consists of a genus name and a species name.
rubric.description: State the two parts of a binomial name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both genus and species.

rubric.why: Standardised scientific names can be used by scientists in different countries.
rubric.description: State that scientific names are used internationally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the worldwide use of the names.

rubric.why: Local names vary and can cause confusion about which organism is meant.
rubric.description: Explain how binomial nomenclature avoids confusion from local names.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking varying local names with confusion.

rubric.why: Scientific names provide a consistent way to identify and classify organisms.
rubric.description: State an identification or classification benefit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that scientific names help identify and classify organisms.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature gives each organism a two-part scientific name: its genus name followed by its species name.
These names are standardised and used internationally, so scientists in different countries can refer to the same organism clearly.
Scientific names prevent confusion caused by different local names for an organism.
They also help identify and classify organisms according to their relationships.

items.followUp: Explain how fermentation by yeast is useful in making bread and alcoholic drinks.

rubric.why: Anaerobic respiration takes place when oxygen is absent or insufficient.
rubric.description: State the oxygen condition for anaerobic respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it occurs in the absence or shortage of oxygen.

rubric.why: Anaerobic respiration releases energy from glucose.
rubric.description: State that anaerobic respiration releases energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying energy release.

rubric.why: Muscle cells can respire anaerobically during vigorous exercise and produce lactic acid.
rubric.description: Give the muscle-cell example and its product.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking muscle-cell anaerobic respiration with lactic acid.

rubric.why: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: State the products of yeast fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both ethanol and carbon dioxide.

rubric.why: The products of yeast fermentation are used in bread-making and in producing alcoholic drinks.
rubric.description: Give a practical use of yeast fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either carbon dioxide making bread dough rise or ethanol being used in alcoholic drinks.

modelAnswer: Anaerobic respiration releases energy from glucose in the absence or shortage of oxygen.
During vigorous exercise, muscle cells may respire anaerobically and produce lactic acid.
In yeast, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
The carbon dioxide makes bread dough rise, and the ethanol is used to make alcoholic drinks.

items.followUp: Give two differences between plant and animal cells.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells lack a true nucleus, whereas eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
rubric.description: Compare the nuclei of the two cell types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles, while eukaryotic cells contain them.
rubric.description: Compare membrane-bound organelles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic DNA is circular, whereas eukaryotic DNA is organised into linear chromosomes.
rubric.description: Compare the form of the genetic material.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller than eukaryotic cells.
rubric.description: Compare the typical sizes of the cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that prokaryotic cells are generally smaller.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotic cells lack a true nucleus; eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells contain membrane-bound organelles.
Prokaryotic cells have circular DNA; eukaryotic DNA is organised into linear chromosomes.
Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller than eukaryotic cells.

items.followUp: Define polymers and give two examples of biological polymers.

rubric.why: Macromolecules are large molecules, often made by joining smaller molecules.
rubric.description: Define macromolecules by their size and the smaller units from which they may be formed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing macromolecules as large molecules formed from smaller molecules.

rubric.why: Proteins and carbohydrates are examples of macromolecules.
rubric.description: Give two examples of macromolecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming any two valid examples.

modelAnswer: Macromolecules are large molecules, often formed by joining many smaller molecules.
Examples include proteins and carbohydrates.

rubric.why: Parasitology is the branch of biology that studies parasites.
rubric.description: Define parasitology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the study of parasites.

rubric.why: Pharmacology studies drugs and their effects on the body.
rubric.description: Define pharmacology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the study of drugs and their effects on the body.

modelAnswer: Parasitology is the branch of biology that studies parasites.
Pharmacology is the branch of biology that studies drugs and their effects on the body.
